title: p0056
universal_lens: Galton's scheme constructs empirical CDFs via order statistics, mapping measurements to percentile grades. The grade operator G(x) = rank(x)/N defines an individual's quantile. Longitudinal tracking compares G_t(x_t) across time. Cross-group comparison aligns distributions via quantile-quantile isomorphism.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats grade G as conformal p-value: P(X ≥ x) = 1 - G(x). Bayesian updating of strength distribution uses Salter's dial likelihood. Posterior predictive grades enable calibrated athlete ranking. Exchangeability across cohorts validates conformal coverage.
gse_mapping: GSE state = (measurement, grade, cohort). Transition: measurement → grade via empirical CDF. Longitudinal drift = ΔG/Δt. Situational reasoning: opponent grade distribution informs contest win probability P(G_self > G_opp). Regime change when measurement instrument recalibrates.

primitives.name: Empirical Distribution Construction
primitives.verbatim_quote: The first step is to marshal our measures in the orderly way familiar to statisticians, which is shown in Table I.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: N: sample size (dimensionless); X_{(i)}: i-th order statistic (same unit as measurement, e.g., kg force); x: measurement value (same unit); F_N(x): empirical CDF (dimensionless, [0,1])
primitives.assumptions: Measurements are independent draws from a fixed distribution; Salter's dial provides ratio-scale measurements; no censoring or truncation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when N is too small for stable quantile estimation (N < 30 for tails); when measurement instrument nonlinearity distorts ordering; when population distribution shifts between measurements.

layer2.mapping: GSI: F_N is the conformal calibration map; GSE: F_N defines the state-space embedding for measurement-to-grade transition.
layer2.telemetry: Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic sup|F_N - F|; quantile estimation error at 0.05/0.95

primitives.name: Grade/Percentile Determination
primitives.verbatim_quote: How shall we determine and specify the Grade that any particular person would occupy in the group?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: x: individual measurement (unit of faculty, e.g., kg force); G(x): grade/percentile (dimensionless, [0,1]); rank(x): integer count (dimensionless); N: group size (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Ties broken by mid-rank convention; distribution continuous enough that ties are rare; grade is invariant to monotonic transformation of measurement scale.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Grade loses resolution at extremes (floor/ceiling effects); when N changes (new entrants), all grades shift; when measurement error σ_meas > inter-quantile spacing.

layer2.mapping: GSI: G(x) = 1 - p-value for conformal prediction; GSE: grade is the sufficient statistic for contest simulation P(win) = G_self * (1 - G_opp).
layer2.telemetry: Grade stability under bootstrap resampling; Spearman correlation between grades at t and t+1

primitives.name: Longitudinal Rank Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: As the years go by, we may learn by the same means whether he is making his way towards the front, whether he just holds his place, or whether he is falling back towards the rear.
primitives.latex: \Delta G_t = G_{t+1}(x_{t+1}) - G_t(x_t), \quad v_G = \frac{dG}{dt} \approx \frac{\Delta G_t}{\Delta t}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t: time (years); x_t: measurement at time t (faculty unit); G_t: grade at time t (dimensionless); ΔG_t: grade change (dimensionless); v_G: grade velocity (per year)
primitives.assumptions: Same measurement instrument and protocol across time; reference population stable or tracked; grade changes reflect true faculty change not population drift.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Population distribution shifts (secular trend) confound individual ΔG; measurement recalibration breaks comparability; regression toward mean creates spurious v_G for extreme initial grades.

layer2.mapping: GSI: v_G is the drift parameter in Bayesian state-space model; GSE: v_G > 0 triggers 'rising star' situational tag, v_G < 0 triggers 'declining' tag.
layer2.telemetry: Autocorrelation of v_G; proportion of variance in ΔG explained by initial G (regression to mean)

primitives.name: Cross-Group Distributional Alignment
primitives.verbatim_quote: Similarly as regards the position of our class, or of our nation, among other classes and other nations.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: F_A, F_B: empirical CDFs of group A and B (dimensionless); p: percentile (dimensionless); x_p: measurement at percentile p in group A (faculty unit); Q_{A→B}: quantile mapping (faculty unit)
primitives.assumptions: Groups measured on same faculty with same instrument; distributions strictly increasing (continuous); quantile-quantile mapping preserves rank-order isomorphism.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Different measurement protocols break unit compatibility; distribution support mismatch (e.g., group B has no individuals at high p); non-monotonic Q-Q plot indicates structural difference not captured by quantile shift.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Q_{A→B} transports conformal prediction sets across populations; GSE: enables fair contest simulation between athletes from different cohorts/leagues.
layer2.telemetry: Q-Q plot linearity (R^2); Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between F_A and F_B ∘ Q_{A→B}

reasoning_traces.think:
Galton's 1884 scheme establishes the empirical distribution function as the sovereign primitive for ranking. The 'marshaling measures in orderly way' (quote 7) is the sort operation yielding order statistics X_{(1)} ≤ ... ≤ X_{(N)}. The grade operator G(x) = rank(x)/N (quotes 5,6) maps any measurement to its quantile, invariant to monotone transformations. This is the exact finite-sample CDF, the nonparametric MLE of the distribution function. Longitudinal tracking (quote 2) defines grade velocity v_G = dG/dt, a dimensionless drift rate. Cross-group comparison (quote 3) uses quantile-quantile transport Q_{A→B}(p) = F_B^{-1}(F_A(x_p)), aligning distributions by rank isomorphism. Salter's dial (quote 4) provides ratio-scale measurements, ensuring grades are meaningful. The breakdown regimes are: (1) small N causing quantile instability, especially in tails; (2) population drift confounding longitudinal v_G; (3) measurement recalibration breaking comparability; (4) support mismatch in cross-group Q-Q mapping. The duality: empirical CDF ↔ quantile function; grade ↔ conformal p-value; longitudinal grade change ↔ state transition in GSE. Failure modes: regression to mean masquerading as v_G; floor/ceiling effects at grade extremes; secular trends requiring detrending before cross-group alignment.
